beats.label: S1 · The pattern
beats.text: MI5 analyst Eve Polastri argues a string of high-profile hits is the work of a single female assassin. Her bosses dismiss her and fire her when the sole witness is murdered.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Eve's obsession and pushes her out of MI5, the precondition for everything after.

beats.label: S1 · Off the books
beats.text: Carolyn Martens of MI6 quietly recruits Eve to hunt the killer, giving her Kenny, Bill and Elena as a covert team. The assassin is Villanelle, handled by a Russian named Konstantin.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the two power centres — Carolyn's off-books unit and Konstantin's handler line — that structure the rest of the season and after.

beats.label: S1 · Bill in Berlin
beats.text: Villanelle lures Eve to Berlin by using her name at a murder scene. Bill tails Villanelle into a nightclub and she stabs him to death on the dance floor.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The first personal cost of the hunt; hardens Eve and marks Villanelle as playing directly at her, not just around her.

beats.label: S1 · The Twelve
beats.text: Frank, Eve's old MI5 boss, is exposed as a paid mole. Before Villanelle silences him he names his employer: a shadow organisation called the Twelve that uses Villanelle for destabilisation.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Twelve as the season's — and the series' — true antagonist, above Konstantin and above Villanelle.

beats.label: S1 · Into her home
beats.text: Villanelle breaks into Eve's flat, eats her dinner and takes her phone. Their hunt tips into something mutual and intimate that neither will name.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The pivot from procedural pursuit to mutual obsession — the engine of every later season.

beats.label: S1 · Carolyn's secret meeting
beats.text: In Moscow, Villanelle kills Nadia inside a prison to stop her talking, then is broken out and handed a new target: Konstantin. Eve discovers Carolyn met Villanelle at that prison before the escape.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Konstantin in Villanelle's crosshairs and plants the first real crack in Carolyn — the reader must carry both suspicions forward.

beats.label: S1 · Paris, the knife
beats.text: Sacked by Carolyn, Eve tracks Villanelle alone to her Paris apartment. They confess their obsession in bed; Eve stabs her, and Villanelle escapes wounded.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the season with the assassin loose, wounded, and now personally betrayed by Eve — the exact state the next season opens from.

cliffhanger.text: Eve has stabbed Villanelle in her own bed after they both admitted the obsession was mutual. Villanelle is alive, wounded, unaccounted for, and no longer being handled by Konstantin — who she was last ordered to kill.
questions: Does Villanelle come back for Eve, or does she vanish?
How far up does the Twelve actually go, and whose side is Carolyn really on?
Is Konstantin dead, in hiding, or still pulling strings?

characters.name: Eve Polastri
characters.line: Former MI5 desk analyst, then Carolyn's off-books investigator, now sacked again after tracking Villanelle to Paris alone and stabbing her.

characters.name: Villanelle
characters.line: The Twelve's star assassin, handled by Konstantin until she was ordered to kill him; last seen fleeing her Paris flat with a knife wound from Eve.

characters.name: Konstantin Vasiliev
characters.line: Villanelle's Russian handler and a Russian Intelligence officer with old ties to Carolyn; shot by Villanelle in the finale and on the run, fearing for his daughter.

characters.name: Carolyn Martens
characters.line: Head of MI6's Russia Section who recruited Eve, then fired her; secretly met Villanelle in the Moscow prison, her loyalties unclear.

characters.name: Kenny Stowton
characters.line: Carolyn's son and the team's researcher on the assassinations; still on Carolyn's side of the operation after Eve is cut loose.

characters.name: The Twelve
characters.line: The shadow organisation named by Frank before his death, funding moles and using Villanelle to destabilise targets across Europe.
characters.note: Never seen directly in S1; only referenced.
